text.p: Bonds were slightly easier in lingering nervousness triggered by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks about inflation still being a risk, but the market lacked any clear direction, traders said.
Traders expected the spread between the 10-year cash and that of the German Bund to continue around 115 basis points, at least until the U.S. market opened.
"The liquidity and the volatility will remain small until the U.S. opens," said one trader.
Traders noted that the escudo was slightly firmer against the mark, ignorning the weakness of the Spanish peseta.
The resilience of the escudo was lending some bond market support. But on the negative side, money market rates were still edging higher, traders said.

Greenspan reaffirmed that the Fed would not hesitate to raise interest rates to cut off any resurgence in inflation but traders said that European investors were still unclear what impact, if any, a U.S. rate rise would have across the Atlantic.
